title: Haptics
summary: Not a screen: the rule for haptics in bipe-app (ADR 0134). Eight haptics named by meaning, played by id from the generated BipeHaptics code, at the uses that registries/haptics.json lists. Bipe has no haptics setting; the phone's system setting wins.

use.description: A use key from the registry, for example message_send, swipe_reply, pin_wrong, web_link_warning.

of.description: One place that plays a haptic.

uses.description: Exactly the uses in the registry. A screen spec that plays one names the use in its notes.

play.effect: Plays the haptic of that use through the generated code. iOS: the UIKit generator the registry names. Android: the first HapticFeedbackConstants entry whose minSdk fits the device.

notes: App code never calls a platform feedback API directly. A new use is a registry line; a new haptic needs an ADR.
iOS plays nothing when System Haptics is off; Android follows the touch feedback setting (design/haptics.md rule 6). No Bipe switch.

Bipe logic: BipeHaptics.play and prepare, and the View modifier in BipeHapticsPlayer.swift (iOS); haptics/BipeHaptics, BipeHapticOnChange, BipeHapticWhen and BipeSwipeHaptics (Android). The registry enum is generated (BipeHaptics in Generated).
